sources.title: 5 Easy Composition Guidelines
sources.author: Diane Berkenfeld
sources.identity: Photographer featured by Nikon USA; the page is a named contributor tutorial on Nikon’s education site.
coverage: rule of thirds and subject placement
sources.trust_reason: Named photographer contributor provides practical composition guidance and examples on Nikon USA’s educational site; wildlife examples require adaptation to people.
sources.read_depth: Opened and read full tutorial text and captions, including Lean Into the Frame (lines 89–111); example pixels not inspected.
sources.notes: For look/action room, text states to direct a person or animal into frame and leave more room toward action. Source examples are wildlife; apply to portraits as an analogy, not as cosplay-specific instruction.

gaps: Coverage now includes edge control, framing, line direction, layers, subject/background separation, silhouette/shape and balance, but Cosplay weapon/wig silhouette management and field-specific prop overlap remain weakly sourced.
No directly inspected specialist tutorial addresses visual shape/rhythm in cosplay portraits or large weapon/accessory framing.
No image pixels were opened; examples and comparisons were inspected via text/captions only.
Chinese-language first-hand composition sources remain limited to one named portrait photographer interview. The institutional university interview-portrait resource timed out.
The source map over-represents Nikon and B&H education; those pages do not all count as independent evidence, and several contributors have limited or unverified professional credentials.
Visual-weight theories are partly author-specific: sources differ over reading direction, placement, foreground prominence and whether balance or expressive imbalance is preferred.

No dedicated professional source found for a universal portrait crop rule tied to cutting at or avoiding a specific joint such as the knee; keep joint-specific advice out of the formal tree unless directly sourced.
